scenes.title: 상자로 고른 후보에서 실제 표면으로
lines: The previous chapter built connections and target bounds. Overlapping bounds select a candidate, but do not yet tell us whether a point reaches the surface.
This chapter has two episodes. First, define the surface orientation, distance and closest point. Next, test whether the point lies within a triangle and calculate its color.

scenes.title: 바닥을 따라가는 화살표와 수직 화살표
lines: A direction along the floor differs from one pointing straight away from it. A plane is a flat surface extending indefinitely; its normal is perpendicular to the surface. The normal itself is not the floor height.

For a floor at height two, choose upward normal zero, one, zero. A dot product multiplies matching components and adds them. This normal leaves only the point's y coordinate, so comparing the result with two tests the floor plane.

scenes.title: 바닥에서 떨어졌다가 표면으로 돌아옵니다
lines: In this Portal 2 preview, bounce from the blue floor and return to a surface. Red follows a visible floor boundary and blue marks the observed moving reference. Screen height is not measured world distance.
Here is another device. Watch the cube leave a faith plate and move toward the button. Travel along a surface differs from travel away from it, which is why we use the normal for distance.

scenes.title: 같은 바닥인데 대입값은 왜 두 배일까요?
lines: The floor is still y equals two. A point at y five is three units away. Multiplying both sides by two gives two y equals four, which describes the same floor.

Substituting five now gives a residual of six. Neither the floor nor the point moved; the equation scale doubled. Undo that scale to obtain perpendicular distance. For a general orientation, the scale is the normal length.

scenes.title: 발판의 위치와 경사를 따로 봅니다
lines: Now watch travel along the orange floor. Its color does not reveal the normal or distance from our previous calculation.
In the next excerpt, a button changes the setup and gel reaches a tilted ramp. A horizontal floor and tilted platform have different orientations. Red follows only the visible platform edge.
Next, cross the gap and reach the other side. Both position and orientation matter. The next explanation moves the same point perpendicularly to find its closest plane location.

scenes.title: 거리에서 실제로 이동할 점으로
lines: We now know the point-to-plane distance. The next question is where to move the point to reach the nearest surface location.

A diagonal path to a flat floor also travels sideways and is longer. The perpendicular path is shortest. For the same floor y equals two, preserve x and z and replace y with two. A unit normal performs that role for a tilted plane.

scenes.title: 표면을 보았으니 법선도 직접 만들 수 있을까요?
lines: So far we chose the normal in advance. Given three vertices, we need to construct an orientation from their coordinates. Use two edges starting at one vertex. This diagram lies in x and y, with z perpendicular to it.

Edges six and four make a rectangle of area twenty-four. Their cross product points perpendicular to both edges; its magnitude is parallelogram area. The triangle has half that area, twelve. Distinguish orientation order from area magnitude.

scenes.title: 방향이 바뀌어도 경계 순서를 따라갑니다
lines: Compare differently oriented panels in several short shots, not one continuous object motion. Lifting or tilting changes the visible edges. Hidden edges are not drawn.

In another excerpt, connect the robot to the device and the wall opens. A plane alone does not define the opening boundary. Next, accumulate boundary vertices in their perimeter order to find orientation.

scenes.title: 세 점에서 여러 꼭짓점의 표면으로
lines: Three points gave a triangle orientation. For a larger boundary with many vertices, an arbitrary selection of three might be almost collinear.

The next method accumulates contributions from neighboring boundary points, returning from the last to the first. Newell names this ordered-boundary method; it is not a method for randomly shuffled points.

scenes.title: 표면까지 왔지만 끝을 넘었을 수 있습니다
lines: This episode defined surface orientation, point-to-plane distance and the closest plane point. We separated residual from distance and checked vertex order.
A plane has no edge. A projected point can lie on the plane beyond the actual platform. Next, carry that point into a finite triangle and describe its location with three numbers.

scenes.title: 평면 위에서 삼각형 안의 주소 찾기
lines: The previous episode found plane distance and the closest point. We now resolve the remaining problem: a point on the plane may still lie outside the platform.

First calculate triangle lengths and area, then locate a point by proportions of its three vertices. Distinguish off-plane from outside-triangle points, and use the same proportions to calculate color.

scenes.title: 넓이는 왜 점의 위치를 구하는 데 필요할까요?
lines: We know the side lengths. Area will let us describe a point in proportions of the three vertices.
The normal example used six and four. Compare the three area formulas on a separate four-by-three triangle; return to six and four for the weights.

scenes.title: 면 위여도 통로 안인지 따로 확인합니다
lines: A turret near a floor portal is drawn into the device. Red marks the visible floor boundary. Knowing plane orientation differs from knowing the finite passage region.
In the next corridor, moving floor and wall portals changes the panels' path. Hide geometry while debris obscures the edges; distinguish corners and interior positions when the surface returns.
A short cooperative excerpt passes through a portal and reaches a finite platform. Notice its edge. Next use triangle area to calculate an interior point's proportions.

scenes.title: 두 점의 보간에서 세 꼭짓점의 비율로
lines: The earlier midpoint mixed two positions equally. Extend that idea to three vertices, returning to the original six-by-four triangle.
Twenty, thirty and fifty percent total one hundred percent. Multiply each position by its proportion and add. These are barycentric coordinates; the name does not require real masses.

scenes.title: 만든 점에서 거꾸로 주소를 읽기
lines: Weights constructed one point eight, two, zero. Recover the weights from that same point and triangle.

The six-by-four triangle has area twelve. Joining the point to the vertices gives subareas two point four, three point six and six. Divide by twelve to recover point two, point three and point five. Keep signed areas to handle outside points.

scenes.title: 그림자의 주소와 물체의 주소는 다릅니다
lines: We found a triangle address. Viewed straight on, a point away from the plane can appear at the same position.

The triangle lies at z zero. One point eight, two, zero and one point eight, two, seven share x and y, but the second is seven units off-plane. Test projected address and coplanarity separately. The shadow analogy explains position overlap, not lighting.

scenes.title: 떠 있는 물체와 바닥의 투영 위치를 구분합니다
lines: The turret rises from the floor toward the device. Apparent overlap with the surface below does not mean it occupies that same plane point. Different colors distinguish the objects.

In the next bright room, a floor portal precedes the robot rising. A triangle traced on visible tile corners is an illustrative projected shape, not the actual game mesh. Test coplanarity and triangle inclusion separately.

scenes.title: 위치를 찾았으니 그 자리의 값도 구합니다
lines: After checking coplanarity and triangle inclusion, determine the value at that location. Reuse the address we just found rather than construct new coordinates.

Store red, green and blue values at the vertices instead of positions. Multiply by the same weights and add to obtain an intermediate color. This is a simple linear color example, not a claim about every displayed color or a game's implementation.

scenes.title: 같은 위치의 표면 값을 따로 생각합니다
lines: Contact the blue-coated platform and move on. Separate the question of surface location from the value stored at that location.
Another excerpt moves a cube through the air. Calculating a surface color still requires identifying which surface position is in question.

Finally observe contact with the blue wall and the resulting bounce. This does not assert the gel effect uses our color formula. Having connected an address to its value, divide larger boundaries into triangles next.
